exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Length of a Side of a Triangle Using the Law of Sines

question.explanation:
First, let's label all of the vertices and sides of our triangle.

The Law of Sines states that \[ \dfrac{x}{\sin{X}} = \dfrac{y}{\sin{Y}} = \dfrac{z}{\sin{Z}}. \]

In this case, we have \[ m\angle{X} = 78^\circ, \quad m\angle{Y} = 36^\circ, \quad x = 16, \] and consequently \[ \dfrac{16}{\sin{78^\circ}} = \dfrac{y}{\sin{36^\circ}}. \]

To solve for $y,$ we multiply both sides by $\sin{36^\circ}$ to give \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \sin{36^\circ} \times \dfrac{16}{\sin{78^\circ}} &= \sin{36^\circ} \times \dfrac{y}{\sin{36^\circ}} \\[5pt] \sin{36^\circ} \times \dfrac{16}{\sin{78^\circ}} &= \cancel{\sin{36^\circ}} \times \dfrac{y}{\cancel{\sin{36^\circ}}} \\[5pt] y &= \sin{36^\circ} \times \dfrac{16}{\sin{78^\circ}}. \end{align*}

Now, $\sin{36^\circ} \approx 0.587\,79$ and $\sin{78^\circ} \approx 0.978\,15,$ both rounded to five decimal places to avoid rounding error. This gives \begin{align*} y &= \sin{36^\circ} \times \dfrac{16}{\sin{78^\circ}} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.587\,79 \times \dfrac{16}{0.978\,15} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{0.587\,79 \times 16}{0.978\,15} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{9.404\,64}{0.978\,15} \\[5pt] &\approx 9.61, \end{align*} rounded to two decimal places.

example.title: Determining the Length of a Side of a Triangle Using the Law of Sines

question.text: The points $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ form a triangle. The points $A$ and $B$ are $20 \, \textrm{m}$ apart. If the measure of the angle at the point $B$ is $47^\circ$ and the measure of the angle at the point $C$ is $62^\circ,$ how far is point $A$ from point $C?$ Round the answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

The Law of Sines states that \[ \dfrac{a}{\sin{A}} = \dfrac{b}{\sin{B}} = \dfrac{c}{\sin{C}}. \]

In this case, we have \[ m\angle{B} = 47^\circ, \quad m\angle{C} = 62^\circ, \quad c = 20, \] and consequently \[ \dfrac{b}{\sin{47^\circ}} = \dfrac{20}{\sin{62^\circ}}. \]

To solve for $b,$ we multiply both sides by $\sin{47^\circ}$ to give \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \sin{47^\circ} \times \dfrac{b}{\sin{47^\circ}} &= \sin{47^\circ} \times \dfrac{20}{\sin{62^\circ}} \\[5pt] \cancel{\sin{47^\circ}} \times \dfrac{b}{\cancel{\sin{47^\circ}}} &= \sin{47^\circ} \times \dfrac{20}{\sin{62^\circ}} \\[5pt] b &= \sin{47^\circ} \times \dfrac{20}{\sin{62^\circ}}. \end{align*}

Now, $\sin{47^\circ} = 0.731\,35$ and $\sin{62^\circ} = 0.882\,95,$ both rounded to five decimal places to avoid rounding error. This gives \begin{align*} b &= \sin{47^\circ} \times \dfrac{20}{\sin{62^\circ}} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.731\,35 \times \dfrac{20}{0.882\,95} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{0.731\,35 \times 20}{0.882\,95} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{14.627}{0.882\,95} \\[5pt] &\approx 16.57, \end{align*} rounded to two decimal places.

example.title: Determining the Length of a Side of a Triangle Using the Law of Sines

question.text: The points $X,$ $Y,$ and $Z$ form a triangle. The points $X$ and $Z$ are $9 \, \textrm{m}$ apart. If the measure of the angle at the point $X$ is $43^\circ$ and the measure of the angle at the point $Y$ is $56^\circ,$ how far is point $Y$ from point $Z?$ Round the answer to one decimal place.
question.explanation:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

The Law of Sines states that \[ \dfrac{x}{\sin{X}} = \dfrac{y}{\sin{Y}} = \dfrac{z}{\sin{Z}}. \]

In this case, we have \[ m\angle{X} = 43^\circ, \quad m\angle{Y} = 56^\circ, \quad y = 9, \] and consequently \[ \dfrac{x}{\sin{43^\circ}} = \dfrac{9}{\sin{56^\circ}}. \]

To solve for $x,$ we multiply both sides by $\sin{43^\circ}$ to give \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \sin{43^\circ} \times \dfrac{x}{\sin{43^\circ}} &= \sin{43^\circ} \times \dfrac{9}{\sin{56^\circ}} \\[5pt] \cancel{\sin{43^\circ}} \times \dfrac{x}{\cancel{\sin{43^\circ}}} &= \sin{43^\circ} \times \dfrac{9}{\sin{56^\circ}} \\[5pt] x &= \sin{43^\circ} \times \dfrac{9}{\sin{56^\circ}}. \end{align*}

Now, $\sin{43^\circ} \approx 0.682$ and $\sin{56^\circ} \approx 0.829,$ both rounded to four decimal places to avoid rounding error. This gives \begin{align*} x &= \sin{43^\circ} \times \dfrac{9}{\sin{56^\circ}} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.682 \times \dfrac{9}{0.829} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{0.682 \times 9}{0.829} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{6.138}{0.829} \\[5pt] &\approx 7.4, \end{align*} rounded to one decimal place.

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Measure of an Acute Angle in a Triangle Using the Law of Sines

question.text: Given that $\angle Z$ is acute, calculate its measure. Round your answer to the nearest degree.
question.explanation:
The Law of Sines states that \[ \dfrac{\sin Z}{z} = \dfrac{\sin Y}{y}. \]

In this case, we have \[ m\angle{Y} = 57^\circ, \quad y = 35,\quad z = 24 \] and therefore \begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin Z}{24} &= \dfrac{\sin 57^\circ}{35} \\[5pt] \sin{Z} &= 24 \cdot \dfrac{\sin 57^\circ}{35} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{24 \cdot \sin 57^\circ}{35} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{24 \cdot 0.838\ldots}{35} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.575, \end{align*} rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, \begin{align*} m \angle{Z} &\approx \arcsin(0.575) \approx \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{35}^\circ, \end{align*} rounded to the nearest degree.

example.title: Determining the Measure of an Acute Angle in a Triangle Using the Law of Sines

question.text: Given that $m \angle A < 90^\circ,$ calculate $m \angle A.$ Round the answer to the nearest degree.
question.explanation:
The Law of Sines states that \[ \dfrac{\sin{A}}{a} = \dfrac{\sin{B}}{b}. \]

In this case, we have \[ a = 20,\quad m \angle B = 35^{\circ},\quad b = 12, \] and therefore \begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin{A}}{20} &= \dfrac{\sin 35^\circ}{12} \\[5pt] \sin{A} &= 20 \cdot \dfrac{\sin 35^\circ}{12} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5 \cdot \sin 35^\circ}{3} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{5 \cdot 0.574}{3} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.957, \end{align*} rounded to five decimal places.

Therefore, \begin{align*} m \angle A &\approx \arcsin(0.957) \approx 73^\circ, \end{align*} rounded to the nearest degree.

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Measure of an Obtuse Angle in a Triangle Using the Law of Sines

question.text: Find, to the nearest degree, the measure of the obtuse angle $X.$
question.explanation:
The Law of Sines states that \[ \dfrac{\sin{X}}{x} = \dfrac{\sin{Z}}{z}. \]

In this case, we have \[ x = 14, \quad m\angle{Z} = 40^{\circ}, \quad z = 10, \] and therefore \begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin{X}}{14} &= \dfrac{\sin{40^\circ}}{10} \\[5pt] \sin{X} &= 14 \cdot \dfrac{\sin{40^\circ}}{10} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{14 \cdot \sin{40^\circ}}{10} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{14 \cdot 0.643}{10} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.900, \end{align*} rounded to $3$ decimal places. This gives \begin{align*} m\angle{X} &\approx \arcsin(0.900) \approx 64.158^{\circ} \end{align*}

But this is less than $90^\circ.$ To get the true value of $X,$ we subtract our answer from $180^\circ\mathbin{:}$ \[ m\angle{X} \approx 180^\circ - 64.158^\circ \approx \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{116}^{\circ}, \] rounded to the nearest degree.

example.title: Determining the Measure of an Obtuse Angle in a Triangle Using the Law of Sines

question.text: Calculate, to two decimal places, the measure of the obtuse angle $B.$
question.explanation:
The Law of Sines states that \[ \dfrac{\sin{B}}{b} = \dfrac{\sin{A}}{a}. \]

In this case, we have \[ b = 9, \quad m\angle{A} = 25^{\circ}, \quad a = 8 \] and therefore \begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin{B}}{9} &= \dfrac{\sin 25^\circ}{8} \\[5pt] \sin{B} &= 9 \cdot \dfrac{\sin 25^\circ}{8} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9 \cdot \sin 25^\circ}{8} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{9 \cdot 0.422\,62}{8} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.475\,45, \end{align*} rounded to $5$ decimal places. This gives \begin{align*} m\angle{B} &\approx \arcsin(0.475\,45) \approx 28.39^{\circ}, \end{align*} rounded to $2$ decimal places. But this is less than $90^\circ.$ To get the true value of $B,$ we subtract our answer from $180^\circ\mathbin{:}$ \[ m\angle{B} \approx 180^\circ - 28.39^\circ \approx 151.61^{\circ} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Applying the Law of Sines when Multiple Triangles are Possible

question.text:
In $\triangle LMN,$ we have $m\angle N = 36^\circ,$ $MN = 9,$ and $LM = 6.$ Which of the following statements could be true?

  1. $\angle L$ is acute
  2. $m\angle L = 75.02^{\circ}$ rounded to $2$ decimal places
  3. $m\angle L = 61.85^\circ$ rounded to $2$ decimal places
question.explanation:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

The law of sines states that \[ \dfrac{\sin{L}}{l} = \dfrac{\sin{N}}{n}. \]

In this case, we have \[ n = 6, \quad m\angle{N} = 36^{\circ}, \quad l = 9, \] and therefore \begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin{L}}{9} &= \dfrac{\sin{36^\circ}}{6} \\[5pt] \sin{L} &= 9 \cdot \dfrac{\sin{36^\circ}}{6} \\[5pt] &\approx 9 \cdot \dfrac{0.587\,79}{6} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.881\,69, \end{align*} rounded to $5$ decimal places. This gives \begin{align*} m\angle{L} &\approx \arcsin(0.881\,69) \approx 61.85^{\circ}, \end{align*} rounded to $2$ decimal places.

In this case, we have \begin{align*} m\angle M &= 180^\circ - m\angle N - m\angle L \\[5pt] &= 180^\circ - 36^\circ - 61.85^{\circ} \\[5pt] &\approx 82.15^\circ. \end{align*}

However, another solution to $\sin{L} = 0.881\,69$ is given by \[ m\angle L \approx 180^\circ - 61.85^{\circ} = 118.15^{\circ}. \]

In this case, we have \begin{align*} m\angle M &= 180^\circ - m\angle N - m\angle L \\[5pt] &= 180^\circ - 36^\circ - 118.15^{\circ} \\[5pt] &\approx 25.85^\circ. \end{align*}

So, there are two possible triangles, with the following angle measures:

  • $m\angle L \approx 61.85^{\circ}, \, m\angle M \approx 82.15^\circ, \, m\angle N = 36^\circ$

  • $m\angle L \approx 118.15^{\circ}, \, m\angle M \approx 25.85^\circ, \, m\angle N = 36^\circ$

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I and III only."

example.title: Applying the Law of Sines when Multiple Triangles are Possible

question.text:
In $\triangle ABC,$ we have $m\angle A = 114^\circ,$ $AC = 5,$ and $BC = 9.$ Which of the following statements could be true?

  1. $\angle B$ is acute
  2. $m\angle C = 44.9^\circ$ rounded to one decimal place
  3. $m\angle B = 30.5^\circ$ rounded to one decimal place
question.explanation:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

The law of sines states that \[ {\dfrac{\sin{B}}{b}} = {\dfrac{\sin{A}}{a}}. \]

In this case, we have \[ a = 9, \quad m\angle{A} = 114^{\circ}, \quad b = 5, \] and therefore \begin{align*} \dfrac{\sin{B}}{5} &= \dfrac{\sin{114^\circ}}{9} \\[5pt] \sin{B} &= 5 \cdot \dfrac{\sin{114^\circ}}{9} \\[5pt] &\approx 5 \cdot \dfrac{0.913\,55}{9} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.507\,53, \end{align*} rounded to $5$ decimal places.

This gives \begin{align*} m\angle{B} &\approx \arcsin(0.507\,53) \approx 30.5^{\circ}, \end{align*} rounded to one decimal place.

In this case, we have \begin{align*} m\angle{C} &\approx 180^\circ - m\angle A - m\angle B \\[5pt] &\approx 180^\circ - 114^\circ - 30.5^{\circ} \\[5pt] &\approx 35.5^\circ. \end{align*}

Another solution to $\sin{B} \approx 0.507\,53$ is given by \[ m\angle B \approx 180^\circ - 30.5^{\circ} \approx 149.5^{\circ}. \]

But we know that a triangle cannot have two obtuse angles. Therefore, there is no triangle that has two angles whose measures are $114^{\circ}$ and $149.5^{\circ}.$

So, there is only one possible triangle, with the following angle measures: \[ m\angle A = 114^\circ, \quad m\angle B \approx 30.5^{\circ}, \quad m\angle C \approx 35.5^\circ \]

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I and III only."
